## Objective
- Build a complete, playable game themed “3D The Sims neighborhood where every house is a Doom level.”

## Requirements
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions.
- For visual checks, save a small JPEG (viewport at most 1280px wide) and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Built a self-contained browser game in a single HTML file using canvas-rendered neighborhood and Doom-like interiors.
- Assumed four selectable homes, each with a distinct basement level, enemies, and simple combat objectives.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added neighborhood UI, selectable homes, canvas-drawn town, four raycast basement levels, movement, shooting, health/ammo, pickups, touch controls, and return/win/lose flows in `index.html`.
- JavaScript syntax check passed.
- Started a local server with `python3 -m http.server 3002`.
- Opened the game in Playwright and saved/inspected `/tmp/opencode/doomington.jpg`.

### Active
- Visual tuning of neighborhood projection; latest edit changed vertical projection in `index.html`, but it has not yet been screenshot-verified.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Reload the page and inspect a new JPEG screenshot after the latest projection edit.
2. Test entering a home, movement, shooting, completion, and mobile layout; fix any issues found.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Complete game implementation; currently the only substantive game file.
- `/tmp/opencode/doomington.jpg`: Latest inspected screenshot, captured before the most recent projection adjustment.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- Playwright browser is available and the local server is running at `http://localhost:3002`.
- Earlier screenshot showed projection issues; code was subsequently adjusted, so that screenshot does not represent the current version.
